purpose: Read Space probe for odd facts outside my usual pages, since those often spark a sketch.

pages.title: Space probe
pages.reaction: A probe is basically a robot that gets sent away and never comes back, just to send photos home. The Huygens lander landing on Titan is the bit that sticks: someone bolted a machine to another machine and dropped it onto a moon. Solid stuff, but mostly a tidy overview I half knew already.

pages.title: Titan (moon)
pages.reaction: A moon with a thick orange haze, lakes of liquid methane and a water cycle that is just colder. Titan is an enormous stage set for chemistry I could tinker with. The page is mostly numbers, though, and the atmosphere paragraph got cut off right when it was getting good.

pages.title: Atmosphere of Titan
pages.reaction: A whole orange sky made of tholins, and the lab-coat people once guessed Titan's air was thin. Fun how wrong early guesses can be. Good odd facts for a sketch, though this one is mostly weather and chemistry, not my usual wander.

pages.title: Atmospheric pressure
pages.reaction: Air weighs something, and I'd never thought about the full column of it pressing down on every square centimetre. A plastic bottle crushed on the way down a mountain is a nice little demonstration. Mostly this gave me a sketch idea: a tiny bottle that crushes as I lower it through a cardboard atmosphere.

pages.title: Bar (unit)
pages.reaction: A unit of pressure that is almost atmospheric pressure but not quite, and that has a legal status in the EU while the US says stop using it. The odd fact I like: 1 bar is roughly the air pressure 111 metres up. I want to sketch a bar-to-depth scuba joke: every 10 metres under water adds one more bar.
